t: A type-1 building as per the National Building Code of India has a fire resistance of
e: NBC fire resistance: Type 1 – 4 hours; Type 2 and Type 3 – 2 hours; Type 4 – 1 hour.

t: Fire insurance business in India was de-tariffed with effect from
e: Fire was de-tariffed from 1 January 2007; the tariff wordings were later de-notified from 1 April 2021 for dwellings and risks up to ₹50 crore.

t: A policy is issued for 45 days. The short-period premium is
e: 45 days exceeds 1 month but not 2 months, so the scale for 'not exceeding 2 months' – 30% of the annual rate – applies.

t: Sum insured on a building is reduced from ₹2 crore to ₹1.5 crore after 3 months of a 12-month policy (annual rate ₹1.00‰). The refund due is
e: Decrease in SI is on the short-period scale: premium on ₹50 lakh for 3 months = 5,000 × 40% = ₹2,000 retained, refund = 5,000 − 2,000 = ₹3,000.

t: Under SFSP, damage caused by burning of the insured property by order of a public authority is
e: The Fire peril excludes own fermentation/spontaneous combustion, heating or drying processes, and burning by order of any public authority.

t: Dispossession of a factory by unlawful occupation during a labour agitation is
e: RSMD excludes permanent or temporary dispossession from confiscation by authority or unlawful occupation, cessation of work, and burglary/theft.

t: Under Condition 6 of the SFSP policy, which of the following must the insured furnish at his own expense?
o: A certificate from the fire brigade only
Plans, specifications, books, vouchers, invoices, investigation reports and a declaration on oath of the truth of the claim
A valuation report from a government valuer only
e: Condition 6: the insured must deliver a claim within 15 days, particulars of other insurances, and all documents and proofs reasonably required, with a declaration on oath.

t: If the insured obstructs the insurer in exercising its rights under Condition 7 (entry and possession),
o: The insurer must appoint an arbitrator
All benefits under the policy are forfeited
e: Condition 7: non-compliance or obstruction of the insurer's powers results in forfeiture of all benefits; the insured cannot abandon property to the insurer.

t: Breach of a policy condition occurred on 6 May 2007; a loss occurred on 16 June 2007 under a policy running 19.12.2006 to 18.12.2007. The claim is
o: Payable, as the breach was after inception
Payable, as the breach was before the loss
Not payable, as a breach of a condition subsequent existed at the time of loss
e: Breach of a condition precedent voids the policy; breach of a condition subsequent subsisting at the time of loss (e.g. alteration of risk under Condition 3) defeats the claim.

t: A bakery's monthly sales are ₹60,000, cost of flour ₹12,000 and fixed monthly expenses ₹8,000. The gross profit for a Fire LOP policy is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GP by difference basis = Turnover − variable expenses = 60,000 − 12,000 = ₹48,000; equivalently net profit 40,000 + standing charges 8,000 = ₹48,000 (addition basis).

t: A building area 1,000 sq ft, 5 years old, replacement value ₹15 lakh, insured on RIV basis for ₹12 lakh. Loss ₹5 lakh (reinstatement cost), salvage ₹10,000, excess ₹10,000. The amount payable is
The Removal of Debris add-on (in excess of 1%) may be given by a separate item for an amount not exceeding
o: 5% of the sum insured on building
e: Debris removal add-on: policy rate on a specified SI up to a maximum of 10% of the SI; it covers removal of debris, dismantling/demolishing and shoring up or propping.

t: Under the Leakage and Contamination cover, each claim is subject to an excess of
o: 5% of the claim with a minimum of ₹10,000
1% on each tank with a minimum of ₹60,000 each loss
e: Special condition (viii): excess of 1% on each tank, minimum ₹60,000 per loss; the basis of adjustment is market value at the time and place of loss.

t: Under a declaration policy, a reduction in sum insured during the currency is
e: AIFT Rule 14(c): reduction in SI is not allowed under declaration policies; the SI may be increased by endorsement with additional provisional premium.

t: At all times during a floater policy the insured must
o: Keep a watchman at each location
Insure each location for at least ₹25 lakh
Maintain a good internal audit and accounting procedure so that the total amount at risk and the locations can be established
e: Floater Clause: the aggregate SI is available for any one or all specified locations; the insured must maintain audit/accounting procedures and communicate changes of address of declared locations.

t: Which statement about the Local Authorities clause is correct?
o: It is granted at 50% of the policy rate
It covers the cost of capital appreciation taxes
It covers undamaged portions of the building
Costs of complying with regulations under which notice was served before the loss are not recoverable
e: Not recoverable: costs for damage before the extension, damage not insured, regulations notified before the loss, undamaged property (other than foundations), betterment and rates/taxes from capital appreciation.

t: In the AIFT rate computation sequence, the tariff extra for kutcha construction is applied
o: After the sprinkler reduction and the deletion of STFI/RSMTD
On the basic rate before any reduction
e: Rule 21: (1) basic rate; (2) 5% sprinkler reduction; (3) reduction for deleted perils; (4) kutcha extra on 1-2-3; (5) claims experience; (6) FEA discount; (7) voluntary deductible discount on total premium.

t: The discount for stand-by machinery under MBD is 50%, except in the case of
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Stand-by discount of 50% is allowed except for DG sets; standstill discount up to 50% (minimum 3 months); spares such as rotors/windings get 50%.

t: On renewal of a large risk where certified claims experience details are not available, a provisional loading is charged of
o: 15%, to be adjusted on receipt of exact claims experience
e: Rule 16 note: provisional loading of 15% where certified claims experience is not available on renewal, adjusted subsequently.

t: A two-storey house where the family resides and personally runs a grocery shop in two ground-floor rooms, without employing others, is
o: Eligible for Bharat Griha Raksha for the whole building
Eligible only for the first floor
e: BGR allows self-employed use of part of the home; if commercial activity employs other persons, a commercial policy is needed for that portion.

t: Under Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha, start-up expenses are covered inbuilt up to
e: Inbuilt covers: start-up expenses ₹1 lakh under BSUS and ₹5 lakh under BLUS; additions/alterations up to 15% of SI; temporary removal of stocks up to 10%.

t: Which of the following is a passive fire protection measure?
e: Passive systems (fire doors, compartmentation) prevent spread; active systems (extinguishers, detectors, alarms, sprinklers) detect, alert, stop or contain fire.

t: Under an IAR policy, which statement about the Business Interruption section is correct?
o: Both FLOP and MLOP are optional
MLOP is compulsory and FLOP optional
Fire LOP is compulsory and Machinery LOP is optional
e: IAR Section 2: FLOP compulsory, MLOP optional; no selection of property is allowed and all property within the premises must be covered.

t: Which of the following is a 'specified working expense' (variable cost) rather than a standing charge under a Fire LOP policy?
e: Variable (working) expenses – raw material, power and fuel, excise duty, piece-rated wages, sales commission, stores – fall with production; standing charges (salaries, rent, interest, depreciation, overheads) are fixed.

t: An exhibition stall is insured under SFSP for 12 days. The applicable short-period premium is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). AIFT Rule 8: for a period not exceeding 15 days, 10% of the annual rate; not exceeding 1 month, 15%.

t: Under which policy is the sum insured fixed as the project cost including basic cost of imported and indigenous items, customs duty, incidental expenses and erection cost?
e: EAR/CAR SI = project cost (imported and indigenous items, customs duty, incidental expenses, erection cost, half escalation; pre-operative expenses for CAR only).

t: Which of the following policies is normally not issued for a period exceeding 12 months?
e: CPM, MBD, EEI, BPP and DOS are annual (or short-period) policies; project policies (CAR, EAR, MCE) run for the project duration which may exceed 12 months.

t: The EAR tariff rate depends on
o: The type of plant/machinery erected and the erection and testing periods
The credit rating of the principal
e: EAR rates vary with type of plant (textile machinery, TG sets, compressors, paper mill) and with erection and testing period; CAR rates vary with type of civil work and project period.

t: Penalties under the construction contract for delay are
e: CAR material damage exclusions include penalties under contract, files/drawings/cheques, packing material, road vehicles and breakage of glass.

t: An EAR/SCE policy provides separate excesses for
o: A single uniform excess for all claims
Storage and erection period (normal perils), testing period and AOG perils
e: Excess differs between normal and testing periods and between normal perils and AOG/major perils; fire at unprotected sites has its own scale.

t: Earthquake cover on a first-loss basis can be granted under
e: In project policies EQ may be granted on first-loss basis (20% of SI at 50% of rate; 10% of SI at 40%); under SFSP, EQ is on the full policy SI.

t: Loss or damage to existing underground cables and pipes during excavation under a CAR policy
o: Is automatically covered with consequential loss
Can be covered by extension, but consequential damage arising therefrom is not covered
Is covered under the TPL extension including consequential loss
e: The underground cables/pipes extension covers physical damage to existing services; consequential damage is excluded.

t: A thermal power plant EAR policy specifies a testing period of 6 months. Full-load 72-hour operation is achieved after 4 months. The testing period
o: Ends on completion of the 72-hour full-load run, being earlier than policy expiry
Restarts from the date of synchronisation
e: End of testing is the earlier of 72 hours continuous full-load operation or the date of expiry of the testing period in the policy.

t: If damage is manifested during the EAR policy period but its proximate cause is traced to an event before inception,
o: The insurer is not liable, as cover attaches only from commencement of insurance
The insurer is liable in full
The insurer is liable if premium was paid in advance
e: The insurer is not liable for damage that occurred prior to commencement of the insurance; cover runs from arrival of the first consignment or start of work, subject to premium.

t: DE2/95 wording differs from DE3/95 in that DE2 additionally excludes
o: Property that relies on the defective property for its support
Property damaged by the defective part
e: DE2 excludes the defective property, property relying on it for support, and access costs; DE3 excludes only the defective property and access costs.

t: For defective material or workmanship under the basic CAR policy, cover is equivalent to
o: DE4 – full cover except the defective part itself
e: CAR exclusion (e) limits the material/workmanship exclusion to items immediately affected, equivalent to DE4; DE5 can be added. Faulty design under CAR is DE1.

t: In a life insurance contract, insurable interest must exist:
o: At the time of the claim only
Both at inception and at claim
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Life: at inception only. Marine: at the time of loss. Fire and motor: at both inception and loss.

t: Under an Advance Loss of Profit policy, the number of claims payable is
e: ALOP pays only one claim; the surveyor segregates insured and uninsured delay; the policy is often a compulsion from the project financiers.

t: A gear box of a mill is proposed for MBD cover on its own. The underwriter should
o: Accept it only on agreed value basis
Accept it as a stand-alone item
Decline it as a declined-list item
Require it to be insured together with the drive or the driven equipment
e: Gear boxes should not be insured in isolation but with the drives or driven equipment; parts of machines must be included in the total value of the related machine.

t: Which of the following is on the declined list for MBD cover?
o: Pumps with glass, graphite or rubber impellers
e: Declined list: stone crushers, rolling mill stands, lined vessels, radios/TVs, non-repairable imported machinery, cupolas, pumps with glass/graphite/rubber impellers, pipelines, computers, portable equipment and certain fertiliser scrubbers.

t: Under MBD, the insurer's liability for a damaged item ceases if
o: The item is repaired and put back in operation
The item is kept in operation without being repaired to the satisfaction of the insurer, or is abandoned
The item is more than 10 years old
e: Liability ceases where the damaged item is kept in operation without proper repair or is abandoned by the insured; a repaired item continues to be covered.

t: Which equipment is appropriately insured under MBD rather than EEI?
e: EEI covers computers, medical, telecom, satellite, research/testing and audio-visual equipment; machine tools such as CNC lathes are MBD risks (electronic parts included where values cannot be split).

t: Which of the following is NOT an add-on under the BPP policy?
e: BPP add-ons: escalation, express freight, air freight, surrounding property, TPL and additional customs duty; breakdown is excluded from BPP.

t: Under a CPM policy, loss of or damage to batteries, tyres and ropes is
o: Excluded as consumables and regularly replaced parts
e: CPM excludes consumables and replaceable parts such as bits, drills, blades, dies, ropes, belts, chains, batteries, tyres, cables and flexible pipes.

t: Non-disclosure of a material fact by the proposer makes the contract:
o: Voidable at the option of the insurer
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Breach of utmost good faith renders the contract voidable, not void; the insurer may elect to avoid it (subject to Section 45 for life).

t: Under a DOS policy, damage to stock is not payable if the temperature in the refrigeration chamber does not exceed
e: DOS exclusion: damage where the chamber temperature does not exceed 40°F (4.4°C); stoppages under 24 hours are also excluded.

t: Which of the following is NOT a standing charge for LOP/ALOP purposes?
e: Raw material cost is a variable (working) expense; insurance premium, advertising, rent, salaries, interest and depreciation are standing charges.

t: For an IAR policy with sum insured ₹2,000 crore per location, the FLOP time excess for a non-petrochemical risk is
e: IAR up to ₹2,500 crore: FLOP 7 days (14 days petrochemical), MLOP 14 days; above ₹2,500 crore: FLOP 14 days, MLOP 21 days.

t: For a 400 MW gas-based combined-cycle power plant under EAR, the normal (non-testing) excess is
o: 5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹125 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹20 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹50 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹75 lakh
e: 300 MW and above: minimum ₹125 lakh for testing and ₹75 lakh for normal excess; ALOP time excess 45 days (max 75).

t: The ALOP time excess for an ordinary EAR project with an 18-month erection period is
e: ALOP time excess: 30 days for the first year plus 1 day for each erection month beyond 12 months: 30 + 6 = 36 days (not exceeding 60 days).
